inputs.text: A baby stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line at JFK on Thursday, and an ICE agent stepped in. That’s the part worth remembering: when a child was in danger, an agent acted. DHS is right to recognize that quick response. Of course public spaces should be safe and properly managed—but treating the rescue as merely a distraction from overcrowding misses the importance of decisive action and the people willing to take responsibility in a crisis. Families deserve both: orderly, well-run public spaces and capable people ready to protect them.
